entries.note: This is a rooftop-solar dataset and is unrelated to RF evidence or capture.

entries.note: Paper evidence, not a public packet or waveform corpus.

entries.title: Matter protocol PCAPNG traces from Thread and Wi-Fi testbeds
entries.note: The fetcher pins Dataverse release v2: 13 PCAPNG traces and three documentation files. These are baseline protocol/testbed observations without jamming or malicious-cause labels.

entries.title: Liverpool LoRa RF fingerprinting dataset
entries.note: Keep device, session, mobility, LOS/NLOS, and antenna domains disjoint across evaluation roles.

entries.title: Oregon State LoRa RF fingerprinting datasets
entries.note: The corpus is very large; pin its exact public file inventory and terms before acquisition.

entries.title: Bristol LoRa sensor RF fingerprinting dataset
entries.note: IEEE DataPort lists a 63.37 MB raw-I/Q archive but requires login and subscription; do not automate credentials.

entries.title: DeepLoRa RF fingerprinting dataset
entries.note: Do not automate credentials or redistribute; record a local receipt after operator-authorized acquisition.

entries.title: Large-scale LoRa RF fingerprinting paper
entries.note: No canonical downloadable dataset artifact is admitted from this citation alone.

entries.title: SMoRFFI same-model Wi-Fi fingerprinting preprint
entries.note: The paper motivates same-model open-set fingerprinting, but its reported model metrics are not Netbraid results. Use the separately pinned Kaggle v3 artifact for local evaluation.

entries.title: SMoRFFI same-model IEEE 802.11g raw-IQ dataset
entries.note: The fetcher pins Kaggle dataset version 3 and 123 same-model devices. Kaggle publishes no per-file checksums, so the ignored receipt records deterministic local SHA-256 values after download; version pinning is provenance, not publisher-backed artifact integrity. The path-free IQ adapter supports mmap row access, but relation splits remain blocked because publisher metadata exposes no acquisition-session axis.

entries.title: Computer Networks cross-layer research article
entries.note: Use as research context; do not infer dataset availability from the article page.

entries.title: Raw I/Q measurement data and software for GNSS RFF fingerprinting
entries.note: The fetcher pins all three artifacts. The data archive exposes controlled clean/spoof, day, and acquisition-category labels in its encrypted member names; layout profiling does not open payloads or establish physical identity. The archive digest checks transfer integrity only; it is not a tamper label.

entries.title: mmWave IWR1642 jammer and target dataset
entries.note: The exact fetch manifest pins 80 MAT artifacts spanning four receiver elements, two radar regimes, with/without-jammer conditions, and one-to-five-target scenes. These are controlled scenario labels, not malicious-intent or tamper labels; receiver, regime, and target count must remain explicit confounders.

entries.title: Indoor IQ samples under controlled jamming
entries.note: The exact fetch manifest pins one workbook and 31 MAT artifacts. The setup holds transmitter and receiver hardware fixed while varying silent, tone, and Gaussian-noise conditions, distance, power, and five same-model jammer radios. Workbook semantics must be profiled before labels are admitted; controlled jamming does not establish malicious intent.

entries.title: RF fingerprinting in mmWave 5G communications
entries.note: The fetcher pins all seven artifacts. The record supports transmitter-feature evaluation and cites a beam-stealing study, but its public metadata does not establish per-sample attack labels. Archive digests check transfer integrity only.

entries.title: INRIA I/Q Signal Dataset for RF Fingerprinting and Physical Layer Authentication
entries.note: The fetcher pins PLA_dataset.zip. Held-out devices can support open-set authorized/rogue evaluation but do not by themselves assert malicious intent. Archive digests check transfer integrity only.

entries.title: RUFF -- Rotating UWB For Fingerprint
entries.note: The record covers 13 boards across 100 positions. The associated paper establishes identical DWM3001CDK hardware, reuse of the same boards, one fixed receiver and channel 5, and two distinct collection days/distance campaigns. Split by source, campaign-scoped location, and day; the fetcher pins only the two NPY archives and leaves duplicate CSV encodings unfetched.

entries.title: RF Fingerprinting WLAN Dataset
entries.note: The fetcher pins both environment archives. Profile their labels before deciding whether same-source cross-environment pairs exist; the record metadata alone does not establish that oracle. Archive digests check transfer integrity only.

entries.title: RFID-ExSim controlled scenario dataset
entries.note: The fetcher pins the sole Zenodo ZIP. The record describes JSONL RFID read events, but the ZIP contains only README.md, LICENSE, and rfid_dataset.png; its README links the complete dataset externally. Zenodo declares no record-level license, so dataset redistribution terms remain unverified. Scenario labels are controlled evaluation oracles and do not establish production intent.

entries.title: IPIN 2015 Track 3 UJIIndoorLoc Wi-Fi fingerprint dataset
entries.note: The fetcher pins the 2015 Track 3 archive from UCI. Evaluation must keep anonymized user, phone, timestamp, building, and floor axes explicit rather than treating the publisher train/validation files as a leakage-safe split.

entries.title: IDLab multi-technology sub-GHz IQ dataset
entries.note: The publisher describes RTL-SDR IQ at 2.048 MHz for LoRa, Sigfox, IEEE 802.15.4g/SUN-OFDM, IEEE 802.11ah, and noise at 864.0 and 867.4 MHz. The external share still needs a bounded artifact inventory, byte extents, format checks, and reviewed local digests before acquisition or evaluation. This can test signal-family recognition, not packet decoding or physical-device identity.

entries.title: Cyber4OT ICS network traces
entries.note: The exact curated-eval manifest pins both publisher artifacts. Keep the staged campaign and related traces in one role: endpoints, trace names, and attack phase otherwise leak the relation target. Publisher scenario labels support protocol-state evaluation, not claims about operator identity or intent.

entries.title: IEC 60870-5-104 intrusion detection dataset
entries.note: The exact curated-eval manifest pins all 14 publisher artifacts. Full captures, protocol-filtered captures, entity views, and derived flow tables from one scenario must stay together so duplicate observations are not counted as independent evidence. Scenario labels do not by themselves establish tamper or malicious intent.

entries.title: Bluetooth channel sounding IQ across diverse scenarios
entries.note: The exact curated-eval manifest pins all four publisher artifacts. Repeated measurements at one geometry are one dependence group; split by scenario and geometry rather than rows, and retain the publisher's differing indoor and outdoor position precision.

entries.title: Sigfox and LoRaWAN fingerprint-localization datasets
entries.note: The exact curated-eval manifest pins all three publisher CSV files. Devices, temporal blocks, geographic cells, gateway geometry, and urban or rural regime must remain explicit grouping axes. RSSI supports localization and tracking evidence, not physical-source identity.

entries.title: EyeFi vision and Wi-Fi trajectory matching dataset v2
entries.note: The exact curated-eval manifest pins the v2 archive. Keep complete source files, days, reboot intervals, phone holders, and environments in one role; do not reuse the publisher's shuffled file order as chronology. Trajectory correspondence is an event-performer relation, not durable person identity.

entries.title: RoboLoc-G multisensor localization dataset
entries.note: The exact curated-eval manifest pins all 26 publisher artifacts; the CSV, ground-truth, and gantry subset is the first evaluation tranche. Hold out complete trajectories and takes, bind coordinate transforms and the documented time offset as calibration provenance, and compare every fused result with its best single sensor.

entries.title: WiSig Wi-Fi RF fingerprinting dataset
entries.note: The public-corpus fetcher pins four processed publisher archives with reviewed local digests. Keep transmitter, receiver, day, capture, and preprocessing stage explicit; frame-level random splits would leak the physical source and receiver chain.

entries.title: Gotham 2025 emulated IoT dataset
entries.note: The public-corpus fetcher pins the publisher archive. Per-device capture and table projections must stay with their orchestration run; emulated device labels support distributed-observer and chronology evaluation, not physical-source identity.

entries.title: Data4Cyber cyber-physical distribution-grid dataset
entries.note: The public-corpus fetcher pins the reviewed release and its current profiler establishes only structural synchronization evidence. Keep complete scenario runs and transition buffers together; attack-phase labels qualify controlled cause, not artifact tamper, physical identity, authorization, or intent.

entries.title: NetsLab 5G O-RAN intrusion-detection dataset
entries.note: The public-corpus fetcher pins the benign archive and two publisher summary databases, but the record does not state a dataset license. The network summary lacks a time axis, so no cross-layer event join is currently established; preserve that negative result rather than fabricating correspondence.

entries.title: UNSW TON_IoT heterogeneous cybersecurity dataset
entries.note: UNSW grants academic research use but requires author permission for commercial use. Its official download is a mutable SharePoint folder without one publisher-pinned artifact inventory, size, or digest, so automated acquisition remains disabled until those terms and files are admitted explicitly.
